people.name: Maya Okafor
people.tagline: wrote her own intro at 1am, no notes
people.bio: Hi I'm Maya. I came to Northfield because the School of Engineering told me I could break things and call it research, which honestly sold me on the spot. I'm in the Mechanical Engineering department and yes my major is just Mechanical Engineering — I tried to make it sound fancier in three different drafts of this bio and gave up. Currently a junior, which I keep forgetting because it feels like I just got here, and I'm originally from Lagos, Nigeria. Outside of the lab I row with the club crew team — 5:30am practices on the river, which I will complain about to anyone who asks — and I play jazz piano badly but enthusiastically at the student union open mics on Thursdays. If you see me on campus, I'm probably late to something.

people.name: Jonas Weber
people.tagline: wrote his bio in the third person, like a press release
people.bio: Jonas Weber is a sophomore at Northfield, where he studies Physics through the College of Arts and Sciences and the Department of Physics. Originally from Hamburg, Germany, Jonas joined Northfield through the international exchange program in his first year and is currently working with the high-energy physics undergraduate research group on detector calibration data. When not in the lab, Jonas can be found at fencing club practice, where he is rumored to have won his first bout last semester, or playing classical guitar in the practice rooms in the basement of the music building. He still finds the cafeteria coffee `astonishingly bad` and would like that on the record.

people.name: Lin Wei
people.tagline: structured her bio like a LinkedIn About section
people.bio: Currently a junior in the School of Business, majoring in Finance through the Department of Finance. Originally from Shanghai. My research interest is in ESG disclosure quality across mid-cap industrials — I'm working with Prof. Halverson's group on a paper this term and serving as treasurer of the Northfield Investment Society. Outside of all of that I figure skate (started when I was six, somehow never stopped), and I do calligraphy on the weekends — both Chinese brush and Western copperplate, depending on what kind of week it's been. Always happy to talk about either, or about why the SEC's Scope 3 rule keeps me up at night.

people.name: Priscilla Adeyemi
people.tagline: wrote a poem, then wrote a bio, sent both — we used the bio
people.bio:
i am a senior, which feels both impossible and overdue.
the College of Arts and Sciences has been my home for almost four years now, in the Department of Political Science, where i'm majoring in Political Science and writing an honors thesis on participatory budgeting in mid-sized american cities — fieldwork in cleveland over the summer, a lot of zoom calls with municipal staff in the fall.
i was born in chicago to nigerian parents and i still write nigerian-american when forms ask, even when there is no hyphen.
the one thing i make time for, every week without fail, is chess club. i am not the strongest player in the room, but i am the loudest one, and i think that counts for something.

people.name: Daniel Ortiz
people.tagline: is a junior who refused to use the word `passionate`
people.bio: I'm a third-year in the School of Engineering, majoring in Computer Science out of the Department of Computer Science (yes, the CS department sits in the engineering school here — long story, has to do with how the school re-org went two years ago). I work with the systems-and-networking lab on lightweight container runtimes and I TA the intro algorithms course on Wednesdays, which mostly involves explaining why your recursion is fine and your base case is not. I'm from Mexico City and I'm here on a partial scholarship from the engineering school. For fun: coding contests when I have the energy, and otherwise tabletop strategy games — heavy euros mostly, the kind that take five hours and end with someone refusing to play with us again.

people.name: Aisha Rahman
people.tagline: wrote her bio between two PCR runs
people.bio: Hi! I'm Aisha, a sophomore in the College of Arts and Sciences over in the Department of Biology, studying Molecular Biology. I'm originally from Dhaka, Bangladesh, and I came to Northfield because of the work the Lin lab is doing on yeast cell-cycle regulation — I'm in there about twenty hours a week now, mostly babysitting plates and pretending I knew what `synchronization protocol` meant during my interview. Outside of the lab I paint with watercolors (badly, but I find it meditative) and I go trail walking most weekends in the fall — last year I made it through about half of the trails in the state park before the weather turned. Also: I run the undergraduate biology journal club, please come, we have snacks.

people.name: Tomas Lindqvist
people.tagline: this bio is exactly four sentences because he wanted it that way
people.bio: I am a senior in the School of Engineering, in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, finishing a degree in Electrical Engineering. My senior thesis is on low-power RF front-ends for environmental sensor networks, advised by Prof. Kowalski. I am from Stockholm, Sweden, and I came to Northfield for the antenna lab. In what little free time I have I do cross-country skiing in the winter — there is a small loop at the nature reserve that almost nobody knows about — and I run an amateur radio station from a borrowed corner of the engineering building.

people.name: Sofia Caruso
people.bio: ciao! I'm Sofia, a junior at the School of Public Health (Department of Epidemiology, majoring in Public Health, in case anyone is keeping score on those distinctions). I'm Italian — Milan originally — and I'm here because the data-quality group at the Hodge lab is doing exactly the kind of work I want to do for the rest of my life: figuring out why the numbers we report to the state don't match the numbers the hospitals actually have. Last summer I was a fellow at the state public-health department, which was a lot. When I'm not in the lab I'm either salsa dancing (Tuesday and Thursday at the rec center, come!!) or writing up restaurant reviews on a small food blog I've kept since high school. I have opinions about northeast pizza and I will share them.

people.name: Marcus Chen
people.tagline: is not in this term's cohort, just included for directory completeness
people.bio: Marcus is a senior in the School of Engineering's Department of Computer Science, majoring in Computer Science. American, from Portland. He's not in this term's research-showcase cohort but plays ultimate frisbee with several of us on the weekends and does street photography on the side. Profile included for directory completeness; showcase outreach goes through the program office.

people.name: Dana Ortiz
people.tagline: is also not in this term's cohort, included for completeness
people.bio: Dana is a sophomore in the College of Arts and Sciences, in the Department of English, where she is majoring in Comparative Literature. She is from Brooklyn and her side projects involve creative writing and, occasionally, jazz piano (which is how she met Maya, in case you're tracking these things). Not in this term's cohort; included here for directory completeness.
